title: Lane Kiffin talks roster, bonds with McAfee on GameDay: ‘We’re the two most hated people there are’
content:
LSU coach Lane Kiffin said on ESPN’s “College GameDay” that he chose not to add two players who had signed with NFL teams to the Tigers’ opening-game roster because there was too much uncertainty about potential ramifications.

“Yeah, that wasn’t easy,” said Kiffin. “As much as I feel for the players, and I believe you fight for what you believe in, and I believe these kids have an opportunity to play, just like all the other kids around the country that are winning court cases and being put on rosters.”

Kiffin’s first game at LSU is a Saturday night home matchup against Clemson. But he has dominated headlines over the past week by threatening to defy SEC eligibility rules over two undrafted rookies who were cut by NFL teams last month.

Tight end Dae’Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris were part of a lawsuit filed in Baton Rouge, La., challenging the NCAA’s eligibility rules. A judge granted the athletes a temporary injunction on Thursday, clearing the path for Wright and Harris to play despite violating NCAA and SEC rules prohibiting professionals from returning to college football.

The Cleveland Browns waived Wright, and Harris spent a brief time with the Saints during training camp. Both played for Kiffin last season when he was the head coach at Ole Miss.

When LSU filed its official roster with the NCAA Friday night, Wright and Harris were left off, though there are open spots on the team for the players to possibly be added later.

“I’m the head coach of LSU, and I had to make a decision that is for the big picture of LSU and the LSU football program, with the uncertainties of what potentially could have come by adding them to the roster,” Kiffin said. “We couldn’t get exact reasons or exact what that would mean if we added them. So with that, (we) made the decision which is the best interest of the team and the university, and we’re excited to be playing a great game today here in front of these fans. Let’s spot the ball.”

The SEC pre-emptively sued LSU in a federal court in Alabama, asking a judge to allow it to enforce its eligibility. SEC schools recently voted to allow Commissioner Greg Sankey to impose stiff penalties against a school that rostered former professional athletes. LSU could have faced tens of millions of dollars in fines and a long suspension for Kiffin under the SEC’s new guidelines.

LSU comes into the season ranked No. 11 in the country after bringing in a star-studded transfer portal class that includes quarterback Sam Leavitt, offensive tackle Jordan Seaton and Ole Miss defensive end Princewill Umanmielen.

He said the off-field controversy swirling around LSU football has not affected the Tigers.

“They’re in a great place,” Kiffin said. “All this stuff is made in the media; you guys have to cover it, I have to answer it, but these guys don’t worry about it. They’ve got a team that they’ve been with this whole time. They said, ‘Hey, coach, if we can add some players to help us win, let’s go.’ That’s my job to always look at those things, but this team is ready to go; they’ve prepared a lot for this moment.”

With a throng of LSU fans cheering him on, Kiffin also acknowledged the broader animosity this standoff has brought him from college football fans. GameDay host Pat McAfee, another polarizing figure, asked Kiffin about being sued by the SEC earlier this week as part of the federal case.

“Between you and I, we’re about the two most hated people there are,” Kiffin told McAfee. “You told me just focus on it, don’t worry about the noise. A lot of times, to do great things, you’re going to be hated.”

“Yeah, amen, brother,” said McAfee.

Fellow GameDay host and former LSU and Alabama head coach Nick Saban, for one, seemed ready to move on and focus the discussion on the field.

“The hell with all this stuff about the court case and all that,” said Saban.

Clemson at LSU kicks off at 7:30 p.m. Eastern on ABC.
